meta.description: Frank Sinatra really said it—in a 1963 Playboy interview—but the documented word was 'anything,' not 'whatever,' and he was talking about faith.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'I'm for whatever gets you through the night'?
meta.ogDescription: Yes, it's Sinatra—from his candid 1963 Playboy interview. But he said 'anything,' not 'whatever,' and the line was about faith, not generic life advice.

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.sourceLine: Documented in Sinatra’s February 1963 Playboy interview ↗, where he said “I’m for anything that gets you through the night, be it prayer, tranquilizers or a bottle of Jack Daniel’s.” The version the internet remembers swaps “whatever” for “anything” and drops the surrounding remark about faith — so the sentiment is genuinely his and the wording is nearly verbatim, but the exact popular phrasing is a light paraphrase.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: “anything that gets you through the night”

source.excerpt: “I’m not unmindful of man’s seeming need for faith… I’m for anything that gets you through the night, be it prayer, tranquilizers or a bottle of Jack Daniel’s. But to me religion is a deeply personal thing in which man and God go it alone together, without the witch doctor in the middle.”
trail: Wikiquote’s sourced section ↗ traces the line to Sinatra’s Playboy interview of February 1963, quoting it in full within his remarks on faith.
Reproductions of the interview, such as this Boing Boing transcript ↗, confirm the documented word is “anything” and preserve the religion context.

Popular quote sites circulate the line without its source: Goodreads ↗ carries the fuller “anything” passage uncited, while BrainyQuote ↗ runs the trimmed “whatever” one-liner — the phrasing the internet remembers — with no citation.
source.excerptNote: The line the internet repeats — “I’m for whatever gets you through the night” — is a trimmed, reworded slice of this passage on faith.
source.rightsHolder: Playboy Enterprises and the Estate of Frank Sinatra
source.rightsNote: The statement was first published in Playboy in February 1963, so it remains under U.S. copyright (works published in 1963 are still protected). The interview text is controlled by Playboy Enterprises, and Sinatra’s words are administered by his estate.

author.bio: Frank Sinatra (1915–1998) was one of the best-selling and most influential entertainers of the 20th century — a singer and Academy Award–winning actor whose recordings and Rat Pack persona made him an enduring American icon. His candid 1963 Playboy interview on religion and faith was among the franker celebrity statements of its era, drawing both praise and outrage.

misattribution.heading: The catch: reworded and stripped of context
misattribution.intro: The quote is authentically Sinatra’s — but the version that circulates online has been lightly reworded and cut loose from what he was actually talking about.

items.why: The documented 1963 wording is “I’m for anything that gets you through the night”; the popular “whatever” is a later synonym swap, per Wikiquote’s sourced entry ↗.

In the interview the line is a comment on faith and organized religion — it follows “I’m not unmindful of man’s seeming need for faith” — yet quote sites present it as free-standing life advice, per this interview transcript ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: Sinatra really said it, in his February 1963 Playboy interview ↗ — but he said “anything,” not “whatever,” and he was talking about faith.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Sinatra’s February 1963 Playboy interview was a rare, unusually blunt celebrity statement on organized religion. The “gets you through the night” line came inside a passage arguing that faith is a private matter between a person and God, “without the witch doctor in the middle.”

Sinatra anticipated the backlash himself, predicting “crank letters, curses, threats” and even a boycott of his records and films. Decades later the line survives online mostly as breezy self-help — its original edge, and its subject, largely forgotten.
